rows.title: Book Event with Mahmoud Khalil
rows.description:
Click here for tickets!

Join AROC Action and the Center for Constitutional Rights for a conversation with Palestinian organizer and writer Mahmoud Khalil on political repression, Palestine solidarity, and the fight against authoritarianism in the United States and around the world.

The discussion will mark the publication of Khalil’s first book, No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention, a memoir drawing on his prison diary and recounting his arrest, incarceration, separation from his family, and continuing struggle against deportation. The book can be purchased for a discount with your ticket, or separately at retail value by clicking below.

rows.title: Grace Krilanovich in conversation with Kate Folk
rows.summary: 20 years after her cult classic The Orange Eats Creeps, Grace Krilanovich ("singular, mistress of a pitiless psychedelic noir lurking in our american woods just beyond the back window.” —Steve Erickson) returns with new novel Acid Green Velvet, in which two young vagabonds in 19th century California navigate class struggle, fringe societies, American identity, and the threat of a menacing man. Also scary dogs. She'll be here in conversation with Kate Folk (“[Folk] writes witty, cinematic fiction that merges familiar scenarios with uncanny menace [and] capably captures the lunacy of the moment we’re living through.”—San Francisco Chronicle) whose latest novel, Sky Daddy, is already a cult classic and an indie bookstore favorite as well!
